newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria in line for $200 mln World Bank loan.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria in line for $200 mln World Bank loan.

text.p: Bulgaria stands to receive $200 million from the World Bank if the government speeds up privatisation, lifts price controls and completes closures of loss-making state firms, a World Bank official said on Sunday.

"We have available for the core adjustment programme up to $200 million of financing...of which $30 million can come forward as a social protection support," World Bank mission leader Kenneth Lay told a news conference.

Speaking at the end of a three-day visit, Lay said he was impressed by the interim government's commitment to leading Bulgaria out of deep economic crisis and speeding up reforms delayed in the past seven years.

He urged the government to consider selling majority stakes in attractive businesses to strategic investors to signal commitment to market reform and thus rekindle the flow of direct foreign investment.

Bulgaria suffers the lowest foreign investment levels in the region and relies solely on external lending for around $1 billion of debt payments due this year, a third of which is in the first quarter.

The government should consider selling whatever share in the Bulgarian Telecommunications Company (BTC) that would bring an optimal price, including to convey shareholders' control, if ncessary sell all of BTC," said Lay.
"We believe this will be a very powerful signal that real reform is under way in Bulgaria," said Lay who is also director of the bank's Southeastern Europe Department.
Bulgaria has so far planned to sell a 25 percent stake in BTC.
Lay also urged the government to liberalise prices of grain and other vital commodities and free trade rules in a move to overcome severe shortages.
He said the bank was prepared to provide support for social protection programmes to cushion the impact of higher prices for the poor.
Bulgaria's grain supplies are forecast to run out in less than 20 days and the interim cabinet is seeking cash to pay for imports.
Lay said he would seek to mobilise support from other international lenders to haul the country out of crisis. A European Union meeting is scheduled in Brussels on Monday.
"When I go to Brussels we will be able to brief them on the government's thinking on the economic policy and seek ways to mobilise support," said Lay.

To speed up action on reform the World Bank and the government have agreed to set up small joint teams that would focus on issues like financial stabilisation, privatisation and social protection, he said.
The World Bank is prepared to help in privatisation deals which involve granting concessions like the BTC, Sofia Airport and highways, sea and river ports.
The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) suspended funding for Bulgaria last year after the ruling Socialists failed to carry out planned structural reforms.

The Socialists stepped down earlier this month after 30 days of street protests fuelled by economic hardship. They agreed to opposition demands to hold an early general election in April, 20 months before the end of their term.
An IMF negotiation mission is expected to arrive on Monday to resume talks on the implementation of a fixed exchange rate regime that would stabilise the financial system.
